name: Tasks
description: A queue of prompts Claude or ChatGPT does one after another, each in its own chat or continuing the one before. Each queue picks who runs it, and each task can too. Every task reports back how it went: outcome, summary, things to know and follow-ups, in one table with links to the chats. Each project has its own queue, and every run is kept in its history. Claude can queue tasks too, after you review and edit them. Reorganize lets a small AI suggest a better order and grouping for what hasn't run.

tools.description: Reports how the task-queue task this chat is running went. Call it once when the task is done or can't go on (only in a chat that runs a queued task; the instructions say so). The user reads the reports as a table instead of reading the chat. It also takes late reports: an earlier task of this chat that ended without a report (No report, or interrupted) is reported with its taskId, which the instructions and the queue's request name; report those first. It also revises: if the user follows up after you reported and the outcome changes (e.g. the work is now finished), call it again with the task's id; the new report replaces the old one and the status follows it. Only this chat's own tasks. Never change the task queue with jig_set_addon_data: this tool is the only way to report.

outcome.description: done, partial (some of it), failed, or blocked (needs something from the user)

summary.description: What you did and the result, in two or three sentences

notes.description: Things the user should know: decisions you took, risks, anything surprising (short lines)

followUps.description: Follow-up tasks you suggest, each a prompt that could be queued on its own

taskId.description: The task to report when it isn't the one running now: an earlier task of this chat without a report, or one it already reported whose outcome changed (its id, e.g. t3). Leave out for the running task

tools.description: Adds tasks to the user's task queue, which Claude works through one after another, each reporting back. Use it when the user asks to queue work, e.g. one task per spec, document, issue or item of a list. Each prompt must stand alone (it usually runs in a new chat): say what to do and where the material is (file paths). It returns the queue.

tasks.description: The tasks in order: each a prompt string, or { title, prompt, newChat, provider, model } (newChat false continues the previous task's chat; provider "claude" or "chatgpt" and model, e.g. opus, sonnet, sol, only on a task that starts a chat: by default the queue's Runs on)

project.description: The project's name; leave out for this chat's project

sameChat.description: All tasks continue one chat instead of each starting a new one (default false)

parked.description: Park the tasks: they go into the parked pool at the end of the queue, ideas the user keeps for later that never run until the user unparks them. Only when the user asks to park them or keep them as ideas (default false: new tasks land before the parked pool). With sameChat they stay one parked chat (the first continues the last parked chat, or starts one when none is parked); a parked chat is unparked as a whole

start.description: Start the queue right away; only when the user said so

tools.description: Changes tasks that are still queued (not running or finished): their title, their prompt, text appended to the prompt, whether they are left out of the run, whether they are parked (ideas kept in a pool at the end of the queue, never run), whether they continue the previous task's chat (newChat), where they are in the queue (moveTo), and who runs them (provider, model). runsOn changes the whole queue's provider. Moves follow the Queue tab's rules: never above or between tasks that ran, and only parked tasks go into the parked pool at the end (park or unpark with parked); a task that lands inside a chat continues it, between chats it starts its own unless newChat is false; wholeChat moves the task's whole chat, only between chats, or with parked parks or unparks the whole chat together, its order and joins kept. A parked task may continue the parked task before it (a parked chat), but the first parked task always starts a chat, and nothing in the queue continues a parked chat. Edits apply in order and all or nothing: a broken rule changes nothing and says why. Safe while the queue runs: it changes only those tasks, never the queue's status. Always use it instead of jig_set_addon_data for the queue; to delete a queued task use addon_tasks_delete. addon_tasks_list gives the ids.

tasks.description: One entry per task: { id, title?, prompt? (replaces it), append? (added on a new paragraph at the end), leftOut? (not on a parked task), parked? (true parks it: to the end of the parked pool; false unparks it: to the end of the queue before the pool, left out unless leftOut is false), newChat? (false continues the chat of the task before it, true starts a new one; the first task in the queue and the first parked task can't continue), moveTo? ("top", "bottom", { after: id } or { before: id }), wholeChat? (with moveTo: move every task of its chat; with parked: park or unpark every queued task of its chat together), provider? ("claude", "chatgpt", or "default" for the queue's choice; only on a task that starts a chat), model? (e.g. opus, sol; null for the default) }

runsOn.description: The queue's Runs on: who runs its new chats (default: the project's default)

project.description: The project's name; leave out for this chat's project

tools.description: Deletes tasks that are still queued from the user's task queue, e.g. one queued by mistake or no longer needed: by id (addon_tasks_list gives them), several at once, all or nothing; a broken rule deletes nothing and says why. Running tasks, ones that need the user and finished ones are never deleted (finished ones stay as the queue's history). It follows the Queue tab's Remove: when the first task of a chat goes, the next task of that chat starts the chat. The user approves it on a card that names the tasks. Use it instead of leaving a task out or renaming it, and never jig_set_addon_data. It returns the queue.

ids.description: The ids of the queued tasks to delete, e.g. ["t3", "t4"]

project.description: The project's name or id; leave out for this chat's project

tools.description: Marks a task in the user's task queue as done by hand, only when the user asks for it (e.g. "mark t33 done"): for a task that ended in Error or without a report although its work was done (e.g. its chat hit its plan's usage limit before reporting), or Partly done, Failed or Blocked while the rest of its work got done elsewhere (e.g. in a follow-up task). The task becomes Done with the note as its summary, marked as set by the user, not reported by a chat; its chat's own report is kept in its details. Queued, running, skipped and already done tasks are refused. addon_tasks_list gives the ids.

note.description: One line saved as the task's summary, e.g. what was done and where it was committed

project.description: The project's name or id; leave out for this chat's project

tools.description: The user's task queue: each task's status and report summary. By default this chat's project's queue; `project` names another project's (its name or id); `all` lists every project's queue compactly (project name and id, then each task's id, status and title), to find a task anywhere and then change it with addon_tasks_edit and its `project`.

project.description: The project's name or id; leave out for this chat's project

all.description: Every project's queue, one short line per task (id, status, title)
